properties.name: Shittim (Abel-Shittim)
properties.description: Israel's final camp east of the Jordan. Spies sent to Jericho from here.

properties.name: Jordan River Crossing
properties.popup: Miraculous crossing on dry ground - Joshua 3-4
properties.description: The waters stood in a heap as the priests carried the ark across. 12 stones taken as memorial.

properties.name: Gilgal
properties.description: 12 memorial stones erected. Site of circumcision and first Passover in Canaan. Israel's military headquarters.

properties.name: Jericho
properties.description: Tell es-Sultan. First Canaanite city conquered. Walls collapsed on day 7. Only Rahab's family spared.
properties.archaeology: Kathleen Kenyon excavations (1952-58); Bryant Wood's reanalysis supports Late Bronze destruction

properties.name: Ai (Theory 1: Khirbet el-Maqatir)
properties.description: Dr. Bryant Wood identified this site as biblical Ai. Fortress destroyed by fire c. 1400 BC matches biblical timeline.
properties.debate: Ai debate: Wood vs Traditional identification. ABR excavations found Late Bronze destruction matching conquest narrative.

properties.name: Ai (Theory 2: et-Tell)
properties.description: Traditional site proposed by Albright, but problematic: no Late Bronze Age occupation. Name means 'the ruin' - may refer to earlier destruction.
properties.debate: Site was unoccupied 2400-1200 BC, contradicting conquest narrative. Recent scholarship questions this identification.

properties.name: Bethel
properties.description: Modern Beitin. The ambush force hid between Bethel and Ai before the attack.

properties.name: Mount Ebal
properties.popup: Altar of Joshua & covenant renewal - Joshua 8:30-35
properties.description: Adam Zertal discovered a large altar structure (1980s). Law written on plastered stones. Blessings and curses ceremony.
properties.archaeology: Zertal's altar discovery matches Deuteronomy 27 specifications

properties.name: Mount Gerizim
properties.description: Half of Israel stood here for blessings. Opposite Mount Ebal across the valley of Shechem.

properties.name: Gibeon
properties.popup: Hivite deception & sun stands still - Joshua 9-10
properties.description: Modern el-Jib. Gibeonites tricked Israel into a treaty. Later defended when 5 kings attacked. Associated with the Anakim giants.
properties.archaeology: Pool of Gibeon discovered with jar handles inscribed 'Gibeon'

properties.name: Beth Horon (Upper)
properties.description: Modern Beit 'Ur al-Fauqa. Israel pursued the fleeing Amorite coalition through this pass.

properties.name: Valley of Aijalon
properties.description: Modern Yalo. Joshua commanded 'Moon, stand still over the Valley of Aijalon' during the battle.

properties.name: Makkedah
properties.description: Five Amorite kings hid in cave here. Multiple proposed sites in the Shephelah region.
properties.debate: Khirbet el-Qom, Tell Bornat, or el-Mughar proposed. No consensus among archaeologists.

properties.name: Libnah (Theory 1: Tel Burna)
properties.description: Tel Burna shows Late Bronze destruction layer. Currently excavated by Bar-Ilan University.
properties.debate: Strong candidate with LB destruction evidence

properties.name: Libnah (Theory 2: Tell Bornat)
properties.description: Traditional identification, but limited excavation. May be Makkedah instead.
properties.debate: Less evidence than Tel Burna for LB occupation

properties.name: Lachish
properties.description: Tell ed-Duweir. Destruction layer Level VI matches conquest period. Extensive excavations confirm Late Bronze burning.
properties.archaeology: Starkey, Ussishkin excavations. LB destruction c. 1150 BC debated

properties.name: Eglon
properties.description: Multiple candidates proposed. Tell Aitun or Tell el-Hesi in Shephelah region.
properties.debate: Tell el-Hesi was earlier candidate but now questioned

properties.name: Hebron
properties.description: Modern el-Khalil. One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities. Later given to Caleb (14:13-14).

properties.name: Debir (Theory 1: Khirbet Rabud)
properties.description: Moshe Kochavi proposed this site. Has Late Bronze remains and matches geographic description.
properties.debate: Better geographic fit than Tell Beit Mirsim

properties.name: Debir (Theory 2: Tell Beit Mirsim)
properties.description: W.F. Albright excavated this site identifying it as Debir. Now largely rejected due to location.
properties.debate: Too far west; most scholars now reject this identification

properties.name: Hazor
properties.popup: Head of northern kingdoms burned - Joshua 11:1-13
properties.description: Tell el-Qedah. Largest Canaanite city (200 acres). Massive destruction layer with burned palace. Yadin & Ben-Tor excavations.
properties.archaeology: Clear Late Bronze destruction c. 1230 BC. Canaanite statues found decapitated.

properties.name: Waters of Merom
properties.description: Near modern Meiron. Combined armies of northern Canaanite kings gathered here and were routed by Joshua.
